findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how the selector obtains the ACTUAL resolved file path for a `.rebar/prompts/` override, since `prompts.get_prompt` returns a `Prompt` exposing only the packaged `fallback_file`; name the helper (or the override-existence probe: `.rebar/prompts/<criterion_prompt_id(C)>.md`) it uses to git-log the override rather than the packaged file.
evidence: prompts.py:166 `def get_prompt(prompt_id, *, repo_root=None) -> Prompt`
prompts.py:187-198: an override at `.rebar/prompts/<prompt_id>.md` is read into `raw` but `fallback_file` is only assigned the PACKAGED filename (line 196)
prompt_model.py:85 `fallback_file: str | None = None  # packaged *.md used when Langfuse is absent` — the Prompt carries no override-path field
Plan claim: 'It resolves through the registry’s own machinery ... and git-logs whichever file that resolution selected, override or packaged.'
findings.finding: The vintage gate's resolution machinery, as named, does not yield the override file path it needs to git-log. The plan resolves via `criterion_prompt_id(C)` then `prompts.get_prompt(...)` and claims it 'git-logs whichever file that resolution selected, override or packaged.' But `prompts.get_prompt` (prompts.py:166) returns a `Prompt` whose only file attribute is `fallback_file`, which is set solely to the PACKAGED filename (prompts.py:196,242); when a `.rebar/prompts/<id>.md` override is used (prompts.py:187-198) the override path is read but never surfaced on the returned object. So `get_prompt`'s return value cannot tell the selector which of the two files was actually resolved.
findings.location: Approach → Vintage gate; AC-2 ('The gate git-logs the file prompts.get_prompt resolved ... one carrying a .rebar/prompts/ override; ... queried path equals resolved path in both cases')
scenarios: A criterion with a committed `.rebar/prompts/plan-review-<id>.md` override: the selector must git-log the override file, but get_prompt returns fallback_file naming the packaged reviewers/*.md, so a naive read git-logs the wrong file and applies the wrong commit history to the vintage gate.
AC-2's override half fails: 'queried path equals resolved path' cannot be asserted from get_prompt's return value alone.
findings.suggested_fix: Resolve the queried path as: if `Path(repo_root)/.rebar/prompts/{criterion_prompt_id(C)}.md` exists, git-log THAT; else git-log `reviewers/{Prompt.fallback_file}` — mirroring get_prompt's own override-wins ordering (prompts.py:187-198) — and assert that path in AC-2 for both the built-in and override cases.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify that the Pass-2-vector vintage precondition resolves its verifier file through the same registry machinery (e.g. prompts.get_prompt on the resolved verifier prompt id, override or packaged) rather than the hardcoded `plan_review_verifier.md`, and name which verifier prompt (base vs agentic) is authoritative.
evidence: Plan: 'The selector does NOT hand-build that path — a built-in's prompt id is hyphenated while its packaged filename is underscored, so a hand-built path matches nothing and would silently skip every criterion. It resolves through the registry's own machinery, `criterion_prompt_id(C)` then `prompts.get_prompt(...)`'
Plan then hand-names: 'additionally requires postdating `plan_review_verifier.md`'

Two packaged verifier files exist: tests/unit/test_criteria_vocabulary_reviewers.py:34-35 list 'plan_review_verifier.md' AND 'plan_review_verifier_agentic.md' — the plan does not say which the Pass-2 vector's vintage is gated on

A project-override seam exists that a hand-built path would silently ignore: src/rebar/llm/evals/plan_replay/tier1.py:93 references '.rebar/prompts/plan-review-verifier.md'; passes.py:208 shows the prompt id is the hyphenated 'plan-review-verifier'
findings.finding: The Vintage Gate resolves each criterion's rubric file through the registry machinery (criterion_prompt_id -> prompts.get_prompt) precisely to avoid the hyphenated-id vs underscored-filename mismatch and to honor .rebar/prompts/ overrides, but the same section then hand-names the literal file `plan_review_verifier.md` for the Pass-2-vector precondition instead of resolving it the same way — the very hand-built-path antipattern the plan bans one paragraph earlier.
findings.location: Approach → Vintage gate ('A signal read from the Pass-2 vector additionally requires postdating `plan_review_verifier.md`')
scenarios: A repo carries a committed .rebar/prompts/plan-review-verifier.md override: git-logging the hardcoded packaged path returns no history for the override, mis-dating (or silently skipping) the Pass-2 precondition
The agentic verifier (plan_review_verifier_agentic.md) is the one actually driving Pass-2 for a criterion, but the gate checks the non-agentic file's vintage — the wrong vintage is enforced

findings.checklist_item: Add an AC asserting the manifest's criterion set equals effective_routing's uncovered-criteria set for the real corpus run.
evidence: DoD: 'the real-corpus run writes a manifest row for every uncovered criterion'
ACs cover exclusion, gate, tiers, ranks, determinism, and specific zero-candidate reasons, but none asserts that the set of manifest rows equals the set of uncovered criteria from effective_routing
findings.finding: The DoD asserts 'the real-corpus run writes a manifest row for every uncovered criterion' but no acceptance criterion provides a proving command for this completeness claim.
findings.location: Definition of Done vs Acceptance Criteria
scenarios: A criterion silently dropped (neither a candidate nor a zero-candidate row) would satisfy every listed AC yet violate the DoD
findings.suggested_fix: Add: 'The manifest contains exactly one candidate group or zero-candidate row for each criterion effective_routing('.', gate_key='plan_review') reports uncovered; verified by pytest comparing the two id sets.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how the Vintage gate recovers the RESOLVED file path (override or packaged) given that prompts.get_prompt returns a Prompt exposing only `fallback_file` (packaged filename, None when an override wins) and no override path.
evidence: Plan: 'It resolves through the registry's own machinery, criterion_prompt_id(C) then prompts.get_prompt(...), and git-logs whichever file that resolution selected, override or packaged.'

prompts.py:187-198 — when a `.rebar/prompts/<id>.md` override is present, its body is read into `raw`, but the returned Prompt's `fallback_file` is set only from `packaged[prompt_id]` (line 196) and is None when the id is not packaged; the override path is never carried.
prompt_model.py:105-122 — the Prompt dataclass exposes id, text, fallback_file (packaged filename) and no resolved on-disk path field.
AC-2 requires 'one carrying a .rebar/prompts/ override ... queried path equals resolved path' — unsatisfiable from get_prompt's return value as described.
findings.finding: The Vintage gate asserts it can git-log the file `prompts.get_prompt` resolved, 'override or packaged', but the returned Prompt does not expose the resolved override path: get_prompt records only `fallback_file` = the PACKAGED filename, which is None/packaged even when a `.rebar/prompts/` override wins.
scenarios: A criterion with an uncommitted-but-present .rebar/prompts/ override: the selector cannot obtain the override path from get_prompt, so it either git-logs the wrong (packaged) file or fails to derive a path — breaking AC-2 and AC-3 (no-committed-prompt-history).
findings.suggested_fix: Either extend get_prompt/Prompt to return the resolved source path, or have the gate reproduce get_prompt's resolution order explicitly: check `<root>/.rebar/prompts/<criterion_prompt_id(C)>.md` first, else join Prompt.fallback_file to src/rebar/llm/reviewers/; git-log whichever path exists. State that the packaged fallback_file is a bare filename that must be joined to the reviewers dir to become a git-loggable repo path.

findings.checklist_item: Name the reason recorded for a criterion that passes the vintage gate and skip list but produces no qualifying signal.
evidence: 'a row for every criterion that produced none, with the reason'
Named reasons cover only 'no-committed-prompt-history' (Vintage gate) and 'unreliable-criterion' (Skip list)
DoD: 'writes a manifest row for every uncovered criterion' — such a criterion may pass the gate but produce no signal
findings.finding: The zero-candidate 'reason' vocabulary is incomplete: two reasons are named (no-committed-prompt-history, unreliable-criterion) but no reason is specified for a criterion that PASSES the vintage gate and is not skipped yet yields no qualifying signal.
findings.location: Approach — 'plus a row for every criterion that produced none, with the reason'
scenarios: A criterion whose eligible reviews existed but neither fired consensus nor an author-response finding needs a zero-candidate row with an unnamed reason
findings.suggested_fix: Add a reason such as 'no-qualifying-signal' for gate-passing, non-skipped criteria with zero candidates.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how the blocking predicate treats a None/absent `decision_margin` (e.g. a None margin fails the margin condition and caps the fire candidate at advisory), so `abs(decision_margin)` is never applied to None.
evidence: sidecar.py:352-359 — `_decision_margin` returns None (not 0.0) when priority or block_threshold is missing/non-numeric
sidecar.py:705 comment — the persisted `decision_margin` is None in that case, so an offline reader can distinguish 'no margin recorded' from 'exactly on the line'
Plan states the margin gate as `abs(decision_margin)` with no clause for a None margin
findings.finding: The BLOCKING tier predicate requires `abs(decision_margin) >= MIN_MARGIN`, but `_decision_margin` (sidecar.py:344-360) returns None — not 0.0 — whenever a finding's priority or block_threshold is missing or non-numeric, and that None is persisted verbatim into the sidecar record (sidecar.py:705). The plan does not state how a fire candidate with a None/absent margin is tiered; `abs(None)` raises, and the intended fallback tier is unspecified.
findings.location: Approach → 'Tiered bar' ('abs(decision_margin) ... at or above the constant MIN_MARGIN = 0.15')
scenarios: A fire candidate whose recorded finding has no numeric priority or block_threshold reaches the tiering step with decision_margin=None
Corpus rows from older sidecar vintages that predate the block_threshold/priority persistence
findings.suggested_fix: State that a fire candidate with `decision_margin is None` fails the margin condition (treated as below MIN_MARGIN) and is therefore at most ADVISORY, and add an acceptance criterion covering a fire candidate whose recorded finding has no numeric margin.

evidence: 3 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: Derive or justify MIN_MARGIN=0.15 from the corpus flip-rate data, or note it as a tunable and make it a named configurable constant.
evidence: 'the constant MIN_MARGIN = 0.15'
'The margin constant drops findings close enough to block_threshold that a small perturbation flips them.' — states purpose, not how 0.15 was derived
The context derives the noise concern empirically (208/551 flips) but the 0.15 value is not tied to any measurement
findings.finding: MIN_MARGIN = 0.15 is an asserted threshold with no derivation from data and is hardcoded as a constant expected to influence which findings are dropped; the plan gives a rationale ('small perturbation flips them') but no measurement establishing 0.15.
findings.location: Tiered bar — 'abs(decision_margin) ... at or above the constant MIN_MARGIN = 0.15'
scenarios: If 0.15 is too high, real blocking candidates are demoted to advisory; too low, unstable findings become blocking fixtures
findings.suggested_fix: Either cite the measurement that yields 0.15 (e.g. the margin below which the 208/551 flips concentrate) or mark it a module-level tunable with a short rationale so it can evolve without a code edit to selector logic.

findings.checklist_item: State the manifest's serialization format (e.g. JSON schema of fields per candidate and per zero-candidate row) and its output path.
evidence: 'writes a LABELED CANDIDATE MANIFEST — per criterion, each candidate with its direction, tier, signals and rank'
'It emits no YAML' — states what it is not, never what it is
AC11: 'emit a byte-identical manifest ... verified by diff of the two files' requires a defined on-disk format and path
findings.finding: The manifest's serialization format and output path are never specified; the plan says it 'emits no YAML' but never states what format it DOES write or to which path, yet multiple ACs assert over it ('byte-identical manifest', 'the manifest holds the second row's id').
findings.location: Approach ('writes a LABELED CANDIDATE MANIFEST') and Acceptance Criteria (AC1, AC11)
scenarios: Executor must invent the manifest schema and location, and the byte-identical AC is unverifiable without a fixed serialization
findings.suggested_fix: Specify the manifest as a JSON file at a named path, listing per-criterion arrays of candidate objects {direction, tier, signals, rank, review_event_uuid, decision_margin} plus zero-candidate rows {criterion, reason}.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State why MIN_MARGIN = 0.15 is a distinct constant from the existing APPLY_NOW_MARGIN = 0.10 (opposite selection direction), or reuse/reference the existing margin concept to avoid a parallel constant in the same package.
evidence: Plan: 'abs(decision_margin) ... at or above the constant MIN_MARGIN = 0.15'
Existing: plan_review/coach_moves.py:172-175 'APPLY_NOW_MARGIN = 0.10 ... Priority margin below a finding’s block_threshold within which a surviving advisory is bucketed apply-now'
Both operate on priority - block_threshold in the same package (evals/plan_replay reuses coach/sidecar machinery)
findings.finding: The plan mints a new margin constant MIN_MARGIN = 0.15 without acknowledging the existing kin constant APPLY_NOW_MARGIN = 0.10 in plan_review/coach_moves.py, which already parameterizes a priority-vs-block_threshold proximity margin. The two are conceptually adjacent (both measure distance to the block line) though directionally opposite (MIN_MARGIN wants findings far enough from the line to be robust; APPLY_NOW_MARGIN buckets findings close to it). Confirm the separate constant is intentional and not an accidental parallel that should reuse or reference the existing margin concept.
scenarios: A future calibration tweaks the block-line proximity policy and updates only one of the two constants, silently desynchronizing selection from triage.
